newsitem.title: CHINA: China, U.S. car joint venture to set up next month.
newsitem.headline: China, U.S. car joint venture to set up next month.

text.p: A $1.57 billion joint venture between the Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp (Group) (SAIC) and U.S. firm General Motors Corp will be formally set up next month, an SAIC official said on Tuesday.
The joint venture, Shanghai General Motors Corp (SGM), is scheduled to produce its first sedan cars by the end of 1998 or early 1999, said SAIC vice president Jiang Zhiwei.
"The annual output of the venture will reach 30,000 cars before 2000, helping to make SAIC one of the world's top 500 companies," he told reporters.

The venture aims to eventually produce 100,000 cars annually but the timing for reaching this target will depend on market conditions, said Shen Jianhua, director of the president's office of the SAIC.
SAIC and General Motors in March signed the agreement to form the joint venture with each side holding a 50 percent stake, Jiang said.
The Chinese government requires cars produced by the joint venture to have 40 percent local content, he said.
General Motors has promised to provide the latest technology to help in the production of the new vehicle, which the company hopes to sell overseas as well as into the domestic market, Jiang said.

SAIC already has a joint venture with Germany's Volkswagen AG. The Shanghai Volkswagen Automotive Co Ltd produced 200,000 passenger cars in 1996, capturing over 52 percent of the domestic passenger car market last year, he said.
